facts.text: Bucheon sits halfway between Seoul and Incheon, making it a key cultural bridge in northwestern South Korea.
The Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival, launched in 1997, draws genre film lovers every July to the city’s streets.
Bucheon’s Sosa‑Wonsi Line, opened in 2018, connects the city’s Sosa station directly to Ansan’s Choji station on Line 4.
The city’s Bucheon Philharmonic Orchestra performs annually, adding a classical soundtrack to Bucheon’s vibrant arts scene.
Bucheon earned UNESCO Creative Cities Network status in 2017, branding itself as the cultural centre of the Seoul Metropolitan Area.
Bucheon’s northern districts host major manufacturing, while the south, served by Lines 1 and 7, buzzes with dense commercial and residential life.
